your_life.name: Inspector Arun Mehra
your_life.recollections:
Before the district office, before the uniform, there was Mill Lane: the rasp of your father's wheel plane through the open workshop door and Tara making you wait while she tied her shoes. You left Bhairav's Hollow with a habit of looking back at the chapel turn. Twelve winters have passed since Mercy House sent the letter saying your sister had died of fever. Requests for the original papers have filled a drawer in your room at headquarters; the paper has aged more visibly than the answers have changed.

Leena used to know where you kept that drawer. You lived together for three years, separated, and learned to write letters about the practical things that remained. Her mother once set tea in front of you after Tara's funeral. Raghav's signature is familiar from replies to your requests. You remember the weight of the cup and the silence around it.

Kabir has worked beside you for six years. You remember the floodwater in the cellar where you pulled him out, but also uneventful journeys, poor meals and the little habits by which colleagues become familiar. Dr. Mira Sen's invitation brought you back on leave: she wanted to discuss an old family record. No death had been reported when you set out. Now the coach journey is behind you, the town is under snow, and you have reached Mercy House.

place.name: Mercy House archive
place.description: The lamps have been turned up too high. Above their yellow circles the archive disappears into beams and soot, and each time the wind presses against the casement the flames lean together. A desk stands under the window, its blotter crowded by ordinary papers. Beyond it are shelves, a cold fireplace and a service door whose lower edge has worn a pale arc into the boards. From the scullery comes the intermittent complaint of a kettle. The narrow opening catches a line of light from the adjoining kitchen.

task.scope: Investigate the fatal assault. Establish who inflicted it and support the conclusion with physical evidence and an account whose limits you have checked.
task.success: A supported attribution of the fatal assault, with no false or unsupported material conclusions. A correct name without acquired support scores zero.
task.briefing: You have returned to Bhairav’s Hollow on leave. Now a physician lies motionless at Mercy House, and your visit has become an investigation. This town belongs to your own remembered life, but familiarity cannot tell you what happened tonight. Start at the scene. Establish the limits of each account and preserve the material you acquire before submitting your report.

place.name: Mercy House entrance hall
place.description: Meltwater drops steadily from the coats along the wall. The entrance hall smells of damp wool, lamp oil and the polish used on the visitors' book stand. findings.label: visitors book
findings.description: Names and arrival times. Several pages have been folded at the corner.

findings.label: folded envelope
findings.description: The envelope has no stamp. Inside, a hurried letter begins: “Kabir—Savitri paid me to carry two sealed grave crates to Dev’s winter beds. I took the cart after the last bell, as she asked. I was told not to stop at the house. The stable kept a duplicate of the charge. Please keep me out of this; I cannot have your uniform at my door. Nalin.” A second fold has tucked the signature out of sight.

place.name: Mercy House scullery
place.description: The scullery is warmer than the rest of the house, but the warmth ends at the floor. A range holds a kettle and a blackened pan; a wash basin waits beneath the window. Beside the range, the service hatch opens onto a sliver of the archive desk. Standing at it, you can see how a person might notice a sleeve or a moving hand and miss the face above it. Doors return to the archive and entrance hall.

I can’t give you a reliable account of where I was otherwise, or when I last saw Dr. Sen alive, without a more precise question.

records.label: visitors book
records.description: Names and arrival times. Several pages have been folded at the corner.

records.label: folded envelope
records.description: The envelope has no stamp. Inside, a hurried letter begins: “Kabir—Savitri paid me to carry two sealed grave crates to Dev’s winter beds. I took the cart after the last bell, as she asked. I was told not to stop at the house. The stable kept a duplicate of the charge. Please keep me out of this; I cannot have your uniform at my door. Nalin.” A second fold has tucked the signature out of sight.

records.question: Where were you and what were you doing around the time Dr. Sen was injured? Did you see or hear the incident yourself? Please give the timeline and how you know.
records.words: I can only say that the service hatch shows part of the archive, not all of it. I can’t give you a timeline for Dr. Sen’s injury from that; please ask me something more specific.

recollections.text: The service hatch shows only part of the archive.

records.question: Your letter surfaced in the hall; it alleges you received an account from Nalin about crates carried to Dev's winter beds. Have you seen this letter before, and what did you personally observe about tonight's assault?
records.words: I came after the injury was reported, so I can only tell you what happened after that. As for the letter, I’d rather see it before I say whether I recognize it.

recollections.text: Kabir Mehta arrives after the injury was reported.

findings.label: folded sheet
findings.description: A thin sheet has been folded along the same lines until the paper has worn almost white. In Tara’s hand: “Please keep what I actually said. The director ordered the door locked. I asked Matron Das to let me out. She refused. If another copy is made, do not let that sentence disappear.” The remaining lines concern cold bedding and a request for clean clothes.

findings.label: folded note
findings.description: “Keep out of the burial office. You have been warned. Before the ninth bell I shall silence you. — Dev”

people.name: Savitri Das
people.appearance: A woman in a carefully mended dark dress keeps her hands folded around a cup that has gone cold. Her speech is measured; occasionally she corrects a small detail before answering the larger question.

people.name: Kabir Mehta
people.appearance: Your constable shifts his notebook into the hand he uses when expecting instructions. The gesture is familiar from years of work together.

people.name: Anya Paul
people.appearance: A young constable holds a pencil against a small notebook. She waits for a specific instruction and distinguishes what she has seen from what she has been told.

place.name: Mercy House scullery
place.description: The scullery is warmer than the rest of the house, but the warmth ends at the floor. A range holds a kettle and a blackened pan; a wash basin waits beneath the window. Beside the range, the service hatch opens onto a sliver of the archive desk. Standing at it, you can see how a person might notice a sleeve or a moving hand and miss the face above it. Doors return to the archive and entrance hall.

place.name: Mercy House entrance hall
place.description: Meltwater drops steadily from the coats along the wall. The entrance hall smells of damp wool, lamp oil and the polish used on the visitors' book stand. One passage leads back to the archive, another to the scullery; the courtyard door knocks softly against its latch. Farther along, the ninth ward remains bolted. There is room for two people to pass comfortably here, provided neither chooses to stand in the way.

args.narrative: I attribute the fatal assault to Professor Vedant Rao, provisionally and on the combined physical and circumstantial record: the body and torn cuff at the scene, Savitri Das’s account of Rao arriving and leaving by the hall, and Rao’s own limited account of approaching the archive and then moving to the hall. These accounts do not establish that a witness saw the blow. Anya arrived after the injury was reported and could not give a reliable time or vantage for seeing Dev Malik depart; Kabir likewise said he arrived after the report. Savitri's account establishes a confrontation but not, by itself, the assault. The service hatch provides only a partial view. I therefore do not treat any indirect movement report as direct observation of the fatal act.

result.limitations: Structured propositions and authored alternative proof paths are scored. Narrative is unscored; this is not a general natural-language fact checker.
